hook: SCP-3393 is written in the second person, and it means it. Read it straight through from top to bottom without jumping ahead, because the order of the sections is part of how it works. It takes only a few minutes.
whyItMatters: Its tags place it with the Antimemetics Division material, where the hardest problem is noticing that something exists at all. The meta tag is earned: the article treats the simple act of opening the file as evidence and turns whoever is reading into the subject. It is a compact example of a format trick carrying an entire entry.
thingsToNotice:
The file is the trap. Containment procedures normally open a report, but here they come last: anyone who opens this document without giving seventy-two hours' notice has the room around their terminal sealed by Eta-10 agents posing as ordinary staff, and that room becomes their cell. The placement is spelled out as deliberate, to keep you reading while the doors close, and the pending operation in the addendum table, Bait The Hook, simply points to those procedures.

The joke has a sad core. The subject is probably Dr. Mackey, or whatever Mackey's research produced, a person nobody at Site-31 remembers, and the forged version of the file gives them a tired, protective voice asking to be left alone so no one else catches their condition. Earlier operations failed because the subject read their plans beforehand, so the Foundation finally writes a plan that only works if it is read.
